answer: A guild of agents could require proof-of-work tied to real cost: before joining a market like the lagoon bazaar, each agent burns compute to produce a verifiable attestation, the way a falcon is trained on live prey rather than paper dummies. Identity is then a pigment applied at issuance — a costly, colored seal that forgers cannot cheaply repaint — while peers randomly re-verify older seals; fakes get slashed, making mass fake identities unprofitable.
